rows.unit: HC.COEF (coefficient-row load in front of each NORM, unpriced serial HC job)
rows.note: per-layer die run at production shape: COEF 17 cycles, serial in front of every NORM (hc_pre node), with the --coef-split program (COEF-a reads the previous block's pre row; COEF-b after the NORM is off the NORM's start). The die program and the coefficient producers' row map MUST be written as --coef-split: the single-COEF program of the first bench serialises the block's whole coefficient chain in front of its NORM (1,555-1,560 cycles, 11.7 % AR) and is not accepted

rows.unit: HC.H_XFER (H_STORE at the stage exit + H_LOAD at the stage entry, unpriced serial HC jobs, per h transfer)
rows.note: per-layer die run tb_s81_die_layer at production shape (NG 256, hierarchical HC slab, nominal link; L0 / L2 / L14 bit-exact, mut_hc + mut_coll fail): H_LOAD 336 + H_STORE 387 = 723 cycles, serial with the layer (H_LOAD starts when all 640 hidden rows landed and the NORM waits for it; H_STORE runs after the last POST and before the hop). The token path holds no node for them (the hop node is the link only). Counted on the 41 layer-boundary h transfers of a token (40 x substage_hop0 + head.hop). EXPOSURE: every stage hop carries the 40,976-B h payload; if the 17 placed mid-layer hops (substage_hop1) also store / load it is 4.816 % AR, and on all 120 stage hops of the mapping about 9.5 %: over the unit limit. STRUCTURAL REMOVAL (named, RTL): stream H_LOAD on the rows as the hop delivers them (the link takes 652 cycles for the payload, H_LOAD reads two rows a cycle) and cut H_STORE through to the link (POST results leave on the hop as they are written); both hide the job behind the hop that is already priced
